lessons.title: HRA Under the Income-tax Act, 2025: Terms to Know Before You Calculate

body.text: The HRA formula fits on one line. Almost every wrong claim comes from misreading one of its words: salary, rent, period or city. Learn exactly what each term means under the new law and the calculation in Chapter 2 becomes mechanical.

children.text: Your payslip may still say "Exemption u/s 10(13A)". Your HR team may still ask for Form 12BB. A blog post may tell you to check your assessment year. All three labels belong to the Income-tax Act, 1961, which stopped applying to income earned from 1 April 2026. The HRA benefit itself survived almost unchanged, but it now lives under new names and numbers. This lesson translates them, then defines the terms you will use in every calculation.
Old Labels, New Law

markDefs.definition: The law that replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961 from 1 April 2026. It rewrote and renumbered the provisions and replaced "previous year" and "assessment year" with a single "tax year".

children.text: The
Income-tax Act, 2025

applies to income from tax year 2026-27 onwards. Its detailed procedures sit in the Income-tax Rules, 2026, notified in March 2026 to replace the Income-tax Rules, 1962. Use this table to decode any document you receive.

body.text: The new law applies to income earned from 1 April 2026. Rent and HRA for April 2025 to March 2026 are still governed by Section 10(13A) and Rule 2A, including the old four-city list. If you are filing a return for tax year 2025-26 in 2026, use the old rules for that year.

children.text: Term 1: Tax Year

markDefs.definition: Under Section 3 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, the 12-month financial year starting on 1 April. Income earned from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 belongs to tax year 2026-27.

children.text: A
tax year

is the 12 months from 1 April to 31 March, defined in Section 3 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. Everything in your HRA calculation, from HRA received to rent paid, is measured within one tax year. Under the old Act, the same period was called the previous year, and it was assessed in the following assessment year. That double naming confused almost every first-time filer.

cells: Schedule III and Rule 279, eight 50% cities

body.title: Quick Check: Which Rules for February 2026?
body.question: Aditya rents a flat in Pune and is on the old regime. Which percentage applies to the third limit for the rent he paid in February 2026?
options: 50%, because Pune is on the new eight-city list
40%, because February 2026 falls before the new rules took effect
50%, because the new law applies to all returns filed after 1 April 2026
It depends on when his employer processes the claim
body.explanation: February 2026 is part of tax year 2025-26, which is still governed by Rule 2A of the 1962 Rules. Under that rule, only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai get 50%, so Pune is at 40%. The date the return is filed does not matter. What matters is the year in which the income was earned. From April 2026, his Pune rent qualifies for 50%.

children.text: Term 2: HRA Received

markDefs.definition: The part of the tax year during which you occupied the rented accommodation. HRA received, rent paid and salary are all measured for this same period.

children.text: The first limit is the HRA actually received for the
relevant period

. That means the HRA credited in your payslips for the months you lived in the rented home, not the HRA figure printed in your offer letter or CTC breakup. If you took unpaid leave and your HRA was cut for a month, the lower figure is what counts.
Term 3: Salary

This is the term most people get wrong. For HRA, "salary" does not mean your gross pay or your CTC. It has a narrow meaning, set by Rule 279 and by long-settled court rulings on commission, and it drives two of the three limits.

body.title: What "salary" means for the HRA calculation

columns.label: Included
points: Dearness allowance, if your terms of employment provide for it
Commission paid as a fixed percentage of turnover you achieve

columns.label: Not included
points: Special allowance, conveyance and other allowances
Performance bonus and variable pay not linked to a fixed turnover percentage
Perquisites such as a company car or meal cards

body.text: A narrow salary definition cuts both ways. It lowers the "10% of salary" deducted from your rent, which helps you. It also lowers the "50% or 40% of salary" ceiling, which can hurt. Lesson 5 shows when each effect wins.

body.title: Try It: Salary for HRA
body.prompt: Mohit is a sales manager for an FMCG distributor in Jaipur. For tax year 2026-27 he earns basic pay of ₹45,000 a month, dearness allowance of ₹5,000 a month (provided in his appointment letter), special allowance of ₹20,000 a month, a performance bonus of ₹1,00,000, and commission of 2% on his annual sales of ₹30 lakh. What is his annual "salary" for the HRA calculation? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Basic pay ₹5,40,000 plus dearness allowance ₹60,000 plus commission of 2% on ₹30,00,000 (₹60,000) equals ₹6,60,000. The special allowance of ₹2,40,000 and the performance bonus of ₹1,00,000 are left out, even though both are taxable salary in the ordinary sense.

children.text: Term 4: Rent Actually Paid

The second limit uses rent you actually paid for the relevant period, less 10% of salary for that period. "Actually paid" means money that genuinely left your account and reached the landlord. A rent receipt with no matching bank transfer or UPI payment is exactly what the tax department looks for. Some payments linked to renting are not rent at all.

cells: Monthly rent under the rent agreement
The core payment for occupying the home
It is refundable, so it is not a cost of occupation
It is a one-time fee to find the home, not rent
These pay for services you use, not for the home
Rent paid by your employer directly to the landlord
You did not pay it, and the benefit is taxed as a perquisite

children.text: Term 5: Where the Accommodation Is Located

The 50% or 40% choice depends on the city where your rented home is situated, not where your office is. Gurugram, Noida, Navi Mumbai, Thane and Ghaziabad are not on the list, however close they are to a metro. The rule names cities, and the address on your rent agreement decides which one you are in.

body.latex: \text{Exempt HRA} = \min\left(H,\ R - 0.1S,\ pS\right),\quad p = \begin{cases} 50\% & \text{home in one of the eight cities} \\ 40\% & \text{home anywhere else} \end{cases}
body.caption: H = HRA received, R = rent actually paid, S = salary, all for the relevant period

body.title: Quick Check: Office in One City, Home in Another
body.question: Tanvi works at an office in Cyber City, Gurugram, and rents a flat in Vasant Kunj, Delhi. Her colleague Ravi works at an office in Connaught Place, Delhi, and rents a flat in Sector 62, Noida. Which percentage applies to each of them?
options: Both 50%, because both work in the Delhi NCR region
Tanvi 40% and Ravi 50%, based on office location
Tanvi 50% and Ravi 40%, based on where each rented home is
Both 40%, because neither lives and works in the same city
body.explanation: The rule looks at where the rented accommodation is situated. Tanvi lives in Delhi, one of the eight cities, so she uses 50%. Ravi lives in Noida, which is not on the list, so he uses 40%, even though his office is in Delhi.

body.title: Scenario: Same Job, Different Side of the Border
body.scenario: Karan and Sameer both work at the same Gurugram office on identical pay: basic salary ₹80,000 a month and HRA ₹40,000 a month. Both are on the old regime and both pay ₹45,000 a month in rent. Karan rents in Vasant Kunj, Delhi. Sameer rents in Sector 45, Gurugram. Both are in the 30% slab.
body.prompt: Calculate each person's exempt HRA for tax year 2026-27 and the difference in tax it creates.
body.modelAnswer: Annual figures: HRA ₹4,80,000, rent ₹5,40,000, salary ₹9,60,000. For both, limit 1 is ₹4,80,000 and limit 2 is ₹5,40,000 minus ₹96,000 = ₹4,44,000. Karan (Delhi, 50%): limit 3 is ₹4,80,000, so his exempt HRA is ₹4,44,000. Sameer (Gurugram, 40%): limit 3 is ₹3,84,000, so his exempt HRA is ₹3,84,000. Karan's exemption is ₹60,000 higher. At 30% plus 4% cess, that is ₹18,720 less tax for Karan every year, just because of which side of the Delhi border he rents on. If both paid a lower rent, such that limit 2 was below ₹3,84,000, the city would make no difference at all.

body.label: Tax gap from the city alone
body.context: Karan and Sameer: same employer, pay and rent. Only the address of the rented home differs.

children.text: Term 6: Form 124 and Landlord Details

markDefs.definition: The form under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 in which an employee gives the employer evidence of claims such as HRA, home loan interest and deductions, so TDS on salary can account for them. It replaced Form 12BB from 1 April 2026.

children.text: To get the exemption in your monthly TDS, you declare your rent to your employer in
Form 124

, which replaced Form 12BB from 1 April 2026. Two details matter for HRA. If the total rent you pay in the tax year exceeds ₹1,00,000, you must give your landlord's PAN. And you must now state your relationship with the landlord, which is designed to catch rent that is "paid" to a parent or spouse on paper only. Lessons 9, 13 and 14 cover these in depth.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The New Rule Number
body.textWithBlank: The limits and city list for the HRA exemption, earlier found in Rule 2A of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, are now in Rule ___ of the Income-tax Rules, 2026.
body.explanation: Rule 279 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 sets the three limits, the definition of salary and the eight 50% cities for the exemption under Schedule III (Table: S. No. 11) of the Income-tax Act, 2025.

body.title: For the curious: how to read a Schedule III entry

children.text: The 2025 Act moved many exemptions out of long, nested sections and into tables in its schedules. Schedule III lists exemptions linked to salary. Each row names the payment, who can receive it, and the conditions or limits, often by pointing to a rule. HRA sits at serial number 11, and its row refers to the limits prescribed in the rules, which is how Rule 279 comes in.

This structure means a change to the city list or percentages can be made by amending the Rules, without Parliament amending the Act. That is exactly how Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad were added.
Decode Your Own Documents

body.title: Translate Your Payslip and HR Forms
steps: Find the HRA exemption line on your payslip or tax computation sheet and note whether it cites 10(13A) or Schedule III
Check that your HR portal asks for Form 124, not Form 12BB, for tax year 2026-27
Work out your "salary" for HRA: basic, plus DA if your appointment letter provides for it, plus any fixed-percentage commission
List everything you paid for your home last month and separate true rent from deposits, brokerage and bills
Check the city on your rent agreement address, not your office address, against the eight-city list
Add up your expected rent for the tax year and see whether it crosses ₹1,00,000, which means you need your landlord's PAN

cards.definition: The 12 months from 1 April to 31 March under Section 3 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. It replaces "previous year" and "assessment year".
The rule in the Income-tax Rules, 2026 that sets the three HRA limits, defines salary and lists the eight 50% cities. It replaces Rule 2A.
Basic pay, plus dearness allowance if the terms of employment provide for it, plus commission as a fixed percentage of turnover. Other allowances, bonuses and perquisites are excluded.
The part of the tax year during which you occupied the rented home. HRA, rent and salary are all measured for this period.
Rent that genuinely reached the landlord for the home you occupy. Deposits, brokerage and utility bills are not rent.
The 50% or 40% limit depends on the city where the rented home is situated, not the city of your office.
The form to declare HRA and other claims to your employer from 1 April 2026, replacing Form 12BB. It asks for landlord PAN above ₹1,00,000 of annual rent and your relationship with the landlord.

points: From 1 April 2026, HRA exemption is granted by Schedule III (Table: S. No. 11) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and Rule 279 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, replacing Section 10(13A) and Rule 2A
Tax year replaces previous year and assessment year. Income up to March 2026 still follows the old Act and the old four-city list
Salary for HRA means basic, DA if the terms of employment provide for it, and fixed-percentage commission. It is not your gross pay or CTC
Only rent actually paid counts. Security deposits, brokerage and utility bills are not rent
The 50% or 40% limit follows the city where your rented home is, not where you work, and can change your tax by thousands of rupees
Form 124 replaces Form 12BB and requires landlord PAN above ₹1,00,000 of annual rent and disclosure of your relationship with the landlord
